source.title: JPL Small-Body Database, 134340 Pluto, orbit solution (producer R.S. Park, DE441)
source.licenceNote: NASA/JPL numbers published without a licence statement; cited as facts with their source.

plane.note: Heliocentric, mean ecliptic and equinox of J2000, as SBDB states.

parentBody.source: The catalogue's solar GM (src/core/bodies/sun.ts), the JPL value

bodyPhysical.source: JPL Horizons physical data for Pluto 999 (vol. mean radius 1188.3 +- 1.6 km, GM planet 869.326), raw docs/evidence/o019-t078-horizons-20261017T035154Z/pluto-phys.txt

rotation.model: IAU WGCCRE 2015 (Archinal et al. 2018, Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astron. 130:22), as transcribed in NAIF pck00011.tpc
rotation.epoch: J2000 (2000-01-01 12:00 TDB); T in Julian centuries, d in days

model.note: Osculating heliocentric elements at the epoch, propagated about the Sun's GM; the SBDB semi-major axis is kept.

accuracy.comparedWith: JPL Horizons vectors, Sun-centred, ICRF treated as EQJ, geometric, UTC
accuracy.classRule: within one diameter: largest error at most the body's mean diameter; approximate demonstration: at most one tenth of the semi-major axis; otherwise not usable as published
knownLimitations: Osculating elements at one epoch (2016-07-31) about the Sun's GM: no perturbation by Neptune or the other planets, which Horizons includes (Pluto is in 3:2 resonance with Neptune). The error is smallest near the epoch and grows both ways: see the table in docs/MOON_ORBITS.md.
Pluto's body centre is compared; the heliocentric two-body orbit describes the Pluto-Charon barycentre, which differs from the body centre by about 2,100 km.
